archetypes.name: Evaluate a Polynomial with the Remainder Theorem
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §5.5 — Zeros of Polynomial Functions
archetypes.coreConcept: The remainder after division by x-k equals the value f(k).
archetypes.mentalModel: Substituting the divisor's zero into the dividend exposes the leftover constant without carrying out long division.

cognitiveTraps.description: Evaluating at the opposite of the zero of x-k.
Reporting the quotient value instead of the remainder value.

archetypes.figureNone: The item asks for a symbolic remainder; a graph would add no information to the substitution.

archetypes.name: Test a Factor with the Factor Theorem
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §5.5 — Zeros of Polynomial Functions
archetypes.coreConcept: The binomial x-k is a factor of f exactly when k is a zero of f.
archetypes.mentalModel: A proposed linear factor is a zero-test: substitute its root and check whether the output vanishes.
archetypes.governingRelation: x-k is a factor of f(x) iff f(k)=0

cognitiveTraps.description: Testing the opposite sign from the root named by x-k.
Reversing the implication and treating a nonzero remainder as evidence of a factor.

archetypes.figureNone: The test is an exact substitution and a graph would reveal whether the proposed factor works.

archetypes.name: List Rational Zero Candidates
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §5.5 — Zeros of Polynomial Functions
archetypes.coreConcept: For integer coefficients, any rational zero p/q in lowest terms has p dividing the constant term and q dividing the leading coefficient.
archetypes.mentalModel: The theorem narrows the search to a finite candidate list; each candidate still needs to be tested.
archetypes.governingRelation: p/q candidate: p | constant term and q | leading coefficient, with gcd(p,q)=1

cognitiveTraps.description: Treating every Rational Zero Theorem candidate as an actual zero before testing it.
Listing only positive ratios and omitting their negative counterparts.

archetypes.figureNone: The problem asks for algebraic candidates; a graph could disclose actual zeros and distract from the theorem.

archetypes.name: Find Polynomial Zeros
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §5.5 — Zeros of Polynomial Functions
archetypes.coreConcept: Polynomial zeros can be found by using candidate tests and factorization, then solving the remaining factors.
archetypes.mentalModel: Each verified zero creates a linear factor; division lowers the degree until the remaining factors are solvable.
archetypes.governingRelation: f(k)=0 iff x-k divides f(x); factor the quotient to find remaining zeros

cognitiveTraps.description: Accepting a rational candidate without substituting it into the polynomial.
Stopping after one factor and failing to solve the quotient for its other zeros.
When the quotient has both a positive and negative real zero, counting only the positive one as the number of remaining zeros.
cognitiveTraps.trapFormula: remaining real-zero count = positive quotient roots only

archetypes.figureNone: A graph would display the target zeros rather than exercise finding them algebraically.

archetypes.name: Build a Polynomial from Given Zeros
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §5.5 — Zeros of Polynomial Functions
archetypes.coreConcept: A polynomial with specified zeros contains corresponding linear factors; a point or coefficient condition can determine its scale.
archetypes.mentalModel: Turn each zero into a factor, multiply to the required degree, then use the additional condition to determine the remaining coefficient.
archetypes.governingRelation: f(x)=a∏(x-r_i)^{m_i}; a is fixed by a known nonzero value or point

cognitiveTraps.description: Writing x+r for a zero r instead of x-r.
Assuming the leading scale is one without applying the supplied condition.

archetypes.figureNone: The target is an algebraic formula; a graph is unnecessary and could expose the factors.

archetypes.name: Bound Positive and Negative Zeros with Descartes' Rule
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §5.5 — Zeros of Polynomial Functions
archetypes.coreConcept: Sign changes in f(x) bound the number of positive real zeros; sign changes in f(-x) bound negative real zeros.
archetypes.mentalModel: Count sign changes twice: once as written for positive inputs and once after substituting the negative input; each count is an upper bound reducible by an even number.
archetypes.governingRelation: positive zero count = sign changes in f(x) minus an even integer; negative zero count = sign changes in f(-x) minus an even integer

cognitiveTraps.description: Treating the sign-change count as the exact number of real zeros.
Using f(x) sign changes to bound negative roots instead of examining f(-x).

archetypes.figureNone: The question asks for an algebraic upper bound; plotting could reveal the actual count.

archetypes.name: Model and Solve a Polynomial Application
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §5.5 — Zeros of Polynomial Functions
archetypes.coreConcept: A real-world constraint can be expressed as a polynomial equation whose meaningful solutions must satisfy the original quantities and conditions.
archetypes.mentalModel: Translate the relationships into one equation, find its polynomial zeros, then reject roots that violate the modeled domain or constraints.
archetypes.governingRelation: model relation -> polynomial equation f(x)=0 -> retain only roots in the feasible domain

cognitiveTraps.description: Reporting an algebraic root that violates a quantity constraint in the original model.
cognitiveTraps.trapFormula: root x<0 retained for a positive length

cognitiveTraps.description: Solving a polynomial expression without first encoding the stated relationship as an equation.
cognitiveTraps.trapFormula: expression roots reported without model constraint

archetypes.figureNone: The item can be expressed and checked with exact algebra; no spatial figure is needed for its chosen context.
